evaluations.query: interactive CLI confirmation prompt library for Node.js, like a simple yes/no dialog
evaluations.reason: Method B includes GT @inquirer/confirm at #3 and all three are relevant CLI prompt libraries. Method C also recommends strong alternatives including @clack/prompts. Method A's yn is just a parser (not interactive), and v-dialogs is a Vue component — irrelevant for Node.js CLI.

evaluations.query: cross-environment JavaScript test framework that supports both Node.js and browser execution
evaluations.reason: Method B recommends jstest (cross-platform), jasmine-core, and GT jasmine — all directly relevant. Method A also has jasmine-core and mocha, both excellent. Method C recommends backendless SDK and @tago-io/sdk which are not test frameworks at all.

evaluations.query: HTTP request interception and mocking library for JavaScript, intercept fetch and XHR calls
evaluations.reason: Method C has GT @mswjs/interceptors at #1, fetch-mock at #2, and mockttp at #3 — all highly relevant and diverse. Method B is also excellent with msw, fetch-mock, and GT at #3. Method A has GT at #1 but #2 and #3 are webdriver-specific interception tools, less broadly useful.

evaluations.query: Node.js terminal styling library for colored and bold text output in CLI apps
evaluations.reason: Method B has GT kleur at #1, chalk at #2, cli-color at #3 — all perfect matches. Method C also recommends chalk, ansi-colors, and kleur — excellent. Method A has kleur at #1 but chalkercli and chalk-animation are animation libraries, not general styling.

evaluations.query: console logger with emoji or unicode symbols for different log levels like success warning error
evaluations.reason: Method A has GT log-symbols at #1, plus log-utils and emojic — all directly relevant. Method B has GT at #2 with @hazeral/logger at #1 which is less well-known. Method C has GT at #3 but loggerr at #1 is a generic logger without symbol focus.

evaluations.query: JSON templating library to dynamically build JSON structures from input parameters in Node.js
evaluations.reason: All three place GT lang-json at #1. Method A adds json-mask which is somewhat useful for JSON manipulation. Method C has js-templates-generator which is partially relevant. Method B drifts to jschemer and apidoc-swagger which are documentation tools, not templating.
